overview: Long before anyone wires up a sensor breakout board, these four humble parts are usually the first 'components' a beginner actually touches. A resistor limits current (the difference between an LED lighting up nicely and burning out instantly). A capacitor stores a small amount of charge and smooths out voltage bumps (why almost every board has a few scattered near its power pins). A diode lets current flow one way only (protecting a circuit from a reversed battery, or catching a motor's voltage spike). A transistor is a tiny electrically-controlled switch (letting a weak microcontroller signal control a stronger current — the same basic idea a relay uses mechanically instead).
simpleSummary: The basic electronic parts — resistors, capacitors, diodes, transistors — every beginner circuit is built from.

specifications.resistor: Rated in ohms (Ω), color-banded to indicate value; common hobby values 220Ω-10kΩ
specifications.capacitor: Rated in farads (typically µF or pF for hobby use); ceramic (small values, no polarity) or electrolytic (larger values, polarized)
specifications.diode: Rated by forward voltage drop and max current; LEDs are a specialized light-emitting diode
specifications.transistor: Rated by max voltage/current and gain; common hobby types include 2N2222 (NPN) and 2N3906 (PNP)

pinMap.name: Resistor Lead 1
pinMap.function: One terminal of a resistor — no polarity, can be wired either direction.
pinMap.currentLimit: Determined by power rating (typically 1/4W for hobby resistors)
pinMap.gotcha: Color bands encode the resistance value — misreading them (a very common beginner error) means the 'current limiting' resistor might not limit nearly enough.

pinMap.name: Capacitor Lead (+)
pinMap.function: On polarized (electrolytic) capacitors, the positive terminal — usually the longer lead.
pinMap.voltageRange: Up to the capacitor's rated voltage
pinMap.gotcha: Wiring an electrolytic capacitor backwards can cause it to heat up, vent, or in extreme cases burst — always check polarity markings (a stripe on the negative side).

pinMap.name: Capacitor Lead (-)
pinMap.function: Negative terminal on polarized capacitors; ceramic capacitors have no polarity at all.

pinMap.name: Diode Anode
pinMap.function: The terminal current flows IN from — conventional current flows anode to cathode only.

pinMap.name: Diode Cathode
pinMap.function: The terminal current flows OUT to — marked with a stripe on the diode body.
pinMap.gotcha: Reversed diodes simply block current rather than passing it — if a circuit relying on a diode does nothing, check orientation before assuming it's faulty.

pinMap.name: Transistor Base
pinMap.function: The control terminal — a small current/voltage here switches a much larger current between collector and emitter.
pinMap.voltageRange: ~0.6-0.7V above emitter to turn on (silicon BJT)
pinMap.currentLimit: Small — typically driven directly from a microcontroller pin

pinMap.name: Transistor Collector
pinMap.function: One side of the switched current path.
pinMap.voltageRange: Up to the transistor's rated voltage

pinMap.name: Transistor Emitter
pinMap.function: Other side of the switched current path.
pinMap.gotcha: Mixing up collector and emitter (an easy mistake, since the package often looks symmetric) usually makes the transistor fail to switch at all rather than working backwards.

useCases.title: Current-limiting an LED
useCases.scenario: A resistor in series with an LED is the very first circuit most people ever build.

useCases.title: Power supply smoothing
useCases.scenario: A capacitor across a power rail smooths out small voltage dips and noise.

useCases.title: Motor flyback protection
useCases.scenario: A diode across a motor or relay coil catches the voltage spike generated when it's switched off, protecting the driving transistor/IC.

useCases.title: Low-current switch driven by a microcontroller pin
useCases.scenario: A transistor lets a weak GPIO pin switch a stronger current than the pin itself could supply.

oftenConfusedWith: Integrated driver ICs (pre-built versions of what a handful of these discrete parts do together)
oftenUpgradedTo: MOSFETs for higher-current switching than a basic BJT transistor comfortably handles
